10-35.solution: Let Rs. \(x\) be at \(8\%\). Two years' interest: \(0.16x + 0.2(25000 - x) = 4400\), so \(5000 - 0.04x = 4400\) and \(x = 15000\). The \(10\%\) part is Rs. \(10000\), and for 2 years CI minus SI on it is \(10000 \times (0.1)^2 = 100\).

10-39.solution: For 2 years, CI minus SI \(= P\left(\frac{r}{100}\right)^2\): \(6250 \times \frac{r^2}{10000} = 10\), so \(r^2 = 16\) and \(r = 4\%\).

10-43.solution: SI for one year is \(\frac{50}{2} = 25\). The extra Rs. \(2\) in CI is interest on the first year's interest: \(25 \times \frac{R}{100} = 2\), so \(R = 8\%\).
